# Generating Synergistic Formulaic Alpha Collections via Reinforcement Learning

arXiv [2306.12964](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.12964) · v1 2023-05-25 · latest 2023-05-25

> **Machine-extracted method card.** The gloss column was written by `claude-opus-5-5` (effort medium) on 2026-10-23 from the html text of the paper. Every quote was checked by a program to be a passage of that text; the gloss has not been checked by a person. "Not found" means the model did not find the item in the text it was given, not that the paper omits it.

| Field | Gloss | Quote from the paper |
|---|---|---|
| **task** | Mining a synergistic set of interpretable formulaic alpha factors for stock trend forecasting, optimized for the performance of a downstream combination model. | “In this paper, we propose a new alpha-mining framework that prioritizes mining a synergistic set of alphas, i.e., it directly uses the performance of the downstream combination model to optimize the alpha generator.” |
| **architecture** | An RL-based alpha generator produces formulas as RPN token sequences (PPO with invalid action masking, shared LSTM with policy/value heads); a linear alpha combination model maintains a weighted pool of alphas and its IC is the episode reward. | “our alpha-mining framework consists of two main components: 1) the Alpha Combination Model, which combines multiple formulaic alphas to achieve optimal performance in prediction, and 2) the RL-based Alpha Generator, which generates formulaic alphas in the form of a token sequence.” |
| **data** | Chinese A-shares daily price/volume data from baostock; 6 features (open, close, high, low, volume, vwap); CSI300 and CSI500 constituents; target is 20-day return. | “We select 6 raw features as the inputs to our alphas: {open, close, high, low, volume, vwap (volume-weighted average price)}. The target is set to be the 20-day return of the stocks, selling/buying at the closing price” |
| **window** | Train 2009/01/01–2018/12/31, validation 2019/01/01–2019/12/31, test 2020/01/01–2021/12/31. | “The dataset is split by date into a training set (2009/01/01 to 2018/12/31), a validation set (2019/01/01 to 2019/12/31), and a test set (2020/01/01 to 2021/12/31).” |
| **models** | PPO agent with a 2-layer LSTM feature extractor (hidden dim 128, dropout 0.1) and MLP value/policy heads (two hidden layers of 64); linear combination model. | “The LSTM feature extractor used in the RL agent has a 2-layer structure with a hidden layer dimension of 128. A dropout rate of 0.1 is used in the LSTM network. The separate value and policy heads are MLPs with two hidden layers of 64 dimensions.” |
| **baselines** | GP (gplearn) and single-alpha-IC PPO generators, each with top-k and mutual-IC-filter set construction; Qlib end-to-end models XGBoost, LightGBM, MLP. | “To answer Q1, we first compare our framework against several other alpha-mining methods and direct stock trend forecasting baselines, including PPO, GP, MLP, LightGBM, and XGBoost.” |
| **headline_result** | Test-period (2020–2021) mean over 10 runs: CSI300 IC 0.0725, Rank IC 0.0806; CSI500 IC 0.0438, Rank IC 0.0727 — best among all methods. | “\| Ours* \| 0.0725 \| 0.0806 \| 0.0438 \| 0.0727” |
| **costs** | No explicit transaction cost figure; backtest uses top-50/drop-5 strategy limiting daily trades to reduce trading costs. | “We evenly invest across the k stocks if possible, but restrict the strategy to only buy/sell at most n stocks on each day to reduce excessive trading costs. In our experiment, k is set to 50 and n to 5.” |
| **uncertainty** | Non-deterministic experiments run with 10 random seeds; means and standard deviations reported. | “To demonstrate the effect caused by stochasticity in the training process, each experimental combination with an indeterministic training process is evaluated with 10 different random seeds.” |
| **leakage_controls** | Chronological train/validation/test split by date; prices forward-dividend-adjusted relative to 2023/01/15 adjustment factors. | “Regarding dividend adjustment, the price/volume data are all forward-dividend-adjusted respected to the adjustment factors on 2023/01/15.” |
| **limitations** | Combining all generated alphas is impractical due to quadratic cost of mutual IC computation, so pool size is capped. | “Considering time and space complexity, it is impractical to combine all generated alphas together, because to calculate mutual correlation for each pair of factors we need \mathcal{O}(k^{2}) evaluations of mutual IC.” |
| **release** | Code publicly available on GitHub at RL-MLDM/alphagen. | “Our implementation is publicly available22 2 https://github.com/RL-MLDM/alphagen/.” |
